newsitem.title: UK: Stocks decline triggers copper rebound.
newsitem.headline: Stocks decline triggers copper rebound.

text.p: News of a big drop in warehouse copper stocks triggered a rally on the price of the key industrial metal on Tuesday. Short-covering following gains in New York also boosted the benchmark London Metal Exchange (LME) price of copper for three months delivery as high as $1,954 per tonne.
It ended the afternoon easier at $1,949 but still well above Monday's $1,905.

Copper has been languishing under a wave of negative sentiment following the disclosure earlier this year of huge losses by Japan's Sumitomo Corp on unauthorised dealing in the metal. But news that stocks held in LME-supervised warehouses in the last week were lower by 8,625 tonnes suggested to traders that seasonal end-user demand for copper might have begun to kick in. World oil prices paused after hitting their highest since the 1991 Gulf War on Monday.

North Sea Brent Blend crude futures on London's International Petroleum Exchange traded around $24.25 per barrel after closing Monday at $24.49. Low stocks of heating fuel underpinned the rally on crude.
Wall Street's run up to 6,000 has failed to give much cheer to commodity markets aside from oil as booming equities and bonds siphon away speculative money.
Aluminium managed to edge higher as copper rallied but remains around its weakest for 2-1/2 years.
Gold prices were firmer but trade was quiet and forays outside the recent price range looked unlikely, dealers said. Bullion ended in London $381.15 an ounce, a dollar above Monday.
Coffee prices ended mixed after profit-taking on gains recorded on Monday with London robusta type November futures down $7 at $1,520 per tonne. Cocoa was little changed.
